title: Direct and Indirect Speech: Statements — Quiz 123
content:
## Direct and Indirect Speech: Statements

Choose the correct tense when reporting statements.

### Lesson focus

1. The Supreme Court said, “Courts can't be silent spectators when the constitutional rights of citizens are violated.”
2. Roshni says to Kiran, “I shall always be there to help you.”

### Understand the pattern

A present reporting verb such as says does not normally require tense backshift. A past reporting verb commonly does, although statements presented as still true can retain their tense. Tell normally needs a listener; say does not take a bare personal object.

### Worked answers and explanation

The legal statement can be reported as 'The Supreme Court said that courts could not be silent spectators when citizens' constitutional rights were violated'. A continuing-principle reading may retain can and are. Roshni says to Kiran that she will always be there to help her. Here says remains present.

### Try another

Correct: She said me that she was ready.

### Suggested answer

She told me that she was ready; or she said to me that she was ready. Told takes me directly, while said requires to before the listener.
